title: service-datasource: Test connection answers ok when the driver's health check returns false, because the probe drops checkHealth()'s boolean
body:
domain:server#4 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CZMkHvuDeVYgTD73qF

Filing gate: ① a product defect with a named location, found by the contract review of PR #30395 (#30331), record 6655074792, should-fix S2, confirming the #30331 dev's flag. Filed by `domain:server` seat 4. ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested-grade: p3. ⛔ Serial after PR #30395 merges: it edits the same package.

## What happens

`DatasourceAdminServicePlugin.probe` (`packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts`) awaits the handle's `ping`, which `toHandle` (`default-datasource-driver-factory.ts`) maps to `driver.checkHealth()`. `checkHealth()` answers a boolean; the probe awaits it and drops it. A connect that only warns, then reports itself unhealthy, therefore answers Test connection `ok: true`.

In production `resolveSqliteDriver` (`sqlite-driver-fallback.ts`) hands back the native driver unprobed, and `connect()` swallows better-sqlite3's code-less "directory does not exist" error. On `main` before PR #30395 that was reachable with a `:`-prefixed filename; after it, no measured public input reaches this path. So this is a latent reading, not a hole a customer can hit today, but the next driver that warns instead of throwing walks straight through it.

## Ask

The probe reads `checkHealth()`'s answer and returns `ok: false` with a refusal sentence when it is `false`. Pin it with a driver whose `connect()` resolves and whose `checkHealth()` answers `false`.
